A type without an entry stays a row on the activity trail. **Guarantee** - Runs: `link`, in the mutation or action that records the event (`audit.recordBackendEvent`), before its row is written - Delivery: once per event recorded; a notification is delivered in the transaction that records the event, and rolls back with it - Order: before the event is written, and before `onEvent` is scheduled - When it throws: the throw is logged as `notifications.deliver_failed` and the notification goes out without a link; the event is recorded either way - Idempotency: a read only: it can run again for a retried mutation | [src/convex/integrations/notifications.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/convex/integrations/notifications.ts) |

### ChannelHandler

Defined in: [src/convex/notifications.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/convex/notifications.ts)

What a channel does to deliver one notification: the inbox writes its row
in the transaction that recorded the event, and email and push, once
they exist, enqueue their send there. It resolves `true` when the
notification was delivered (or enqueued), and never throws what would
roll the event back: the caller logs a failure and goes on.

### NotificationChannel


Defined in: [src/convex/notifications.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/convex/notifications.ts)

The channels a notification may take. `app` is the inbox; `email` and

***

### NotificationAudience

```ts
type NotificationAudience = "subject" | "inviter" | "entity";
```

Defined in: [src/convex/notifications.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/convex/notifications.ts)

Who a kind notifies:
- `subject`: the account the event is about;
- `inviter`: whoever sent the invitation the event's `targetId` names, while
  they are still a member, else the owners and admins of the workspace it joined;
- `entity`: the owners and admins of the workspace the event names
  (`entityId`), else the account it is about. A billing entity is a
  workspace, or an account billed on its own.

### ChannelGate

```ts
type ChannelGate<Ctx> = (ctx, userId, type, channel) => Promise<boolean>;
```

Defined in: [src/convex/notifications.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/convex/notifications.ts)

The person's own choices and limits for one channel of one kind: `false`
skips it. Notifications ships the answer yes; the preferences replace it
with each person's channel choices, the weekly cap and the quiet hours.
The inbox never waits for a cap or quiet hours: only an explicit choice
turns it off.

## Functions

### setupNotifications()

```ts
function setupNotifications(components, options?): Notifications;
```

Defined in: [src/convex/integrations/notifications.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/convex/integrations/notifications.ts)

The in-app inbox: what the backend recorded about a person, live, with
the unread count and marking read, and the `notify` option that turns
your own events into notifications.

Every event of the package that concerns a person (a role, a passkey, an
invitation, a payment, a gift, a bounce) reaches the inbox with nothing
set up. Your own kinds join through `notify`, and pass the instance to
`setupAudit({ notifications })` so the events you record reach it.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `components` | [`NotificationsComponents`](#notificationscomponents) |
| `options?` | [`SetupNotificationsOptions`](#setupnotificationsoptions) |

#### Returns

[`Notifications`](#notifications)

#### Example

```ts [backend/notifications.ts]
import { setupNotifications } from 'nuxt-backend/notifications'
import { components } from './_generated/api'

export const notifications = setupNotifications(components, {
  notify: { 'app.strip_ready': { channels: ['app'], link: event => `/strips/${event.targetId}` } },
})

export const { listNotifications, getUnreadCount, markNotificationsRead } = notifications.api
```
